feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: Unpacking President Trump's financial stake in Nvidia
entry.summary: NPR's Scott Detrow speaks with Dan Alexander, a senior editor at Forbes and author of a book about President Trump's businesses, about the president's holdings in Nvidia given recent news.

entry.title: After losing federal food aid, more people turn to food pantries this Thanksgiving
entry.summary: Families in rural upstate New York plan for Thanksgiving after losing their SNAP benefits this year because of new work requirements.

entry.title: Doctors struggle to save babies after parents refuse vitamin K
entry.summary: Newborns typically get an injection of vitamin K in the hospital, which can prevent a potentially deadly bleeding condition. But the number of parents refusing the shot is rising.

entry.title: Moving to Florida may become a choice of some Republicans after midterms
entry.summary: In Florida, Republicans kept power of state government after the midterms. It's now the largest state where the GOP is still in charge.

entry.title: Oil slicks in the Strait of Hormuz are harming the environment
entry.summary: More than 600 oil slicks threaten marine life in the Strait of Hormuz as war and tanker attacks turn vital waters into an environmental disaster.

entry.title: These deer walk 300 miles a year. The race is on to save their migration
entry.summary: Mule deer in Wyoming make some of the longest land migrations in the lower 48 states. They're trying to adapt to a changing climate, but growing development could stand in their way.

entry.title: Lawmakers promote use of popular but untested peptides for troops and veterans
entry.summary: Promoters says peptides can build strength and delay aging, but medical experts warn of potential safety risks. Now, there's a push on Capital Hill to allow U.S. troops to use them.

entry.title: How high technology is changing cargo crime
entry.summary: Truckloads of turkey and bourbon are getting stolen in transit. Cargo theft of food and beverages are on the rise in part because the goods are hard to trace. We look at how high technology is changing cargo crime.

entry.title: Many families are cutting corners at the grocery store to pay their other bills
entry.summary: Cash-strapped consumers are changing they way they spend money. As essentials like rent and utility bills gobble up more of their budget, some families are dialing back on groceries or eating out.

entry.title: The Army says there's no reason to panic over controlled ammunition detonation in Iowa
entry.summary: The U.S. Army says it has taken precautions and there's no reason to panic about its' plan to detonate unusable bomb making material at its ammunition plant in Iowa, scheduled for Wednesday morning.
